subject: materials-science
intro: Materials science leads to engineering the substances everything is made of — designing alloys, semiconductors, polymers and composites, then scaling them into real products.

roles.title: Materials Scientists
roles.what: Research the structures and properties of metals, ceramics, semiconductors, polymers and glass, working out how to strengthen, combine or invent materials with the properties new applications need.
roles.where: The course is a materials primer: crystallography and X-ray diffraction (unit 5), defects in solids (unit 6), glassy solids (unit 7), polymers (unit 10) and semiconductors and doping (unit 4).

roles.title: Materials Engineers
roles.what: Evaluate materials and develop the machinery and processes that manufacture them to demanding design and performance specifications — including metallurgists, ceramic engineers and welding engineers.
roles.where: Diffusion in solids and heat treatment (unit 11), phase diagrams (unit 12), failure-fracture-and-fatigue (unit 6) and the metals-ceramics-polymers-composites lesson map directly onto the job.

roles.title: Chemists
roles.what: Conduct qualitative and quantitative chemical analyses and experiments for quality or process control or to develop new products and knowledge — the bench science behind every new material.
roles.where: Aqueous solutions, acids and bases (unit 9) and reaction rates (unit 8), with the atomic-structure and bonding units, are the analytical chemistry a materials lab runs before a device is made.

roles.title: Electrical Engineers
roles.what: Research, design, develop, test or supervise the manufacture of electrical equipment, components and systems — work that rides on the semiconductor physics underlying every modern device.
roles.where: Semiconductors and doping (unit 4) and the chemistry-of-batteries bonus lecture are the direct bridge into electronic devices and energy storage that electrical engineers design and test.

roles.title: Natural Sciences Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate research and development in the physical sciences — deciding which materials projects are pursued and leading the laboratories and teams that carry them out.
roles.where: The course's lab-sequence arc from atomic models through batteries, with computational-materials-design (unit 3), mirrors the industrial R&D programmes such managers set and steer.
